input.rationale: Section 7 contains only a mutual waiver of consequential/indirect damages (carved out for indemnification and breach of confidentiality); no monetary cap on liability appears in Section 7 or anywhere else in the document (searches for "aggregate", "exceed" and "Fees" return no cap language). The fallback requires a mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs, so the absence of any cap fails the fallback on a material term and leaves our own direct liability unlimited. Because this is a revenue-share arrangement in which Customer pays no fees to Kubient (Section 5: payment flows from Kubient to Customer), a pure "fees paid by Customer" basis would be illusory; the redline therefore adopts the preferred greater-of formulation using amounts paid or payable between the Parties and a USD 1,000,000 floor, adds the standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirms revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages" for cap purposes. The existing consequential-damages waiver is mutual and acceptable and is left intact.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs to Section 7
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 waives consequential damages but sets no cap, so both parties' direct liability is unlimited; we add our standard mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' amounts under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and revenue-share amounts owed under Section 5 remain payable.

ops.text: (b) Except with respect to Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the amounts paid or payable between the Parties under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. Amounts owed by a Party under Section 5 (Fees and Payment) shall not be treated as damages subject to this limitation.
